subject: Request: short-term safety buffer for overnight POC soak
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@datacraft.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — overnight soak headroom for latency run

Hi Neha,

Quick context: our engineering team will run a 10-hour overnight soak tonight (10pm PT start) to validate tail latency at higher concurrency for the NLP augmentation pipeline. We surfaced a risk with the current trial allowance — we expect to overshoot by ~120k tokens based on our preflight.

Can Redwood provide a short-lived safety buffer (48h) or promo top-up to avoid the run being cut off mid-test? This is a production-critical validation for our Q3 deployment timeline. If helpful, I can share the exact traffic profile and an estimate sheet.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform — DataCraft
attachments: preflight-traffic-estimate.csv (csv)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — overnight soak headroom for latency run

Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and the estimate (got the CSV). We can likely support a short window of additional tokens, but I need to coordinate with our SE team and get sign-off on promo/top-up policy. Looping in Karthik for the technical sizing and Marissa for approval on the credit memo.

Plan I'm proposing:
- Short-term uplift: 150k tokens credit, 48-hour expiry starting at test kickoff
- Safety cap: auto-disable when measured 95th tail latency exceeds agreed threshold (to protect our infra) — SE can configure
- We will charge nothing for the uplift if run stays within expected profile; otherwise we reconcile after the POC

Karthik — can you confirm the latency guard we should apply (max p95) and whether any model variant fallbacks are required?

Neha
Neha Kapoor

On Sun, Jun 15, 2025 at 10:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik — can you confirm the latency guard we should apply (max p95) and whether any model variant fallbacks are required?

Thanks Neha. Ran the numbers against their CSV. Recommendation below: 
- Safeguard: set a p95 threshold of 250ms on the request path for the test windows; if exceeded for two contiguous 5-minute windows, throttle to a lower-QPS lane and notify the ops channel.
- Model fallbacks: encourage using the quantized-compatible variant (gpt-medium-q4_0) for tail runs; we can transparently route to full model only if latency returns within threshold.
- Token buffer: 150k looks right given peak concurrency in their profile (~600 concurrent streams).

Sanjay — if you confirm you want the fallback route enabled, we will configure routing rules and KV cache warmers before the test starts. Karthik (SE) will be on-call during the soak.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
